subject: Residency evidence & procurement gate — next steps after discovery call
messages:
From: Alex Rodriguez <alex.rodriguez@velatherapeutics.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Jul 2028 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up + compliance checklist (Vela x Redwood)

Olga / Ben — thanks again for the conversation earlier. Quick recap from our side and the immediate asks so we can move procurement forward: 

Summary of our constraints / goals
- Data residency: All PHI/PII must remain in our EU tenancy (Frankfurt region). No persistent copies outside our VPC.
- Isolation: Primary preference is a VPC-hosted deployment (customer-managed VPC peering or PrivateLink). Air-gap is on the table but would be heavier for SOW.
- Egress & network: No unpredictable outbound IPs — we need a short list of static egress IP ranges or NAT gateway workarounds.
- Compliance: SOC 2 Type II and encryption key management (customer-managed KMS) are must-haves for legal review.
- Authentication: SAML/IdP integration and SCIM for user sync.
- Timeline: procurement team wants an evidence package + a draft SOW to satisfy our security gate by 7/20.

Attached is our internal compliance checklist (Vela-Compliance-Checklist.xlsx) — can you confirm which items Redwood can cover out-of-the-box vs. items that require an add-on or custom work? 

Next steps we’d need from you this week: 
1) A short evidence bundle (SOC2 summary, network approach, KMS options).
2) Static egress IP ranges or recommended connectivity architecture.
3) Draft SOW or procurement template so our buyers can start redlining.

Also looping in Karen (legal) separately — she may join the next call. Thanks,

— Alex
Alex Rodriguez
CTO, Vela Therapeutics
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rodriguez <alex.rodriguez@velatherapeutics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 6 Jul 2028 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Follow-up + compliance checklist (Vela x Redwood)

Alex — really great conversation, appreciate the clear list. Quick recap + what we’ll deliver before your procurement gate.

Call recap (short)
- You’re evaluating a VPC-hosted private deployment in eu-west-1 (Frankfurt).
- Hard constraints: no persistent copies outside customer VPC for regulated workloads; customer-managed KMS; SOC2 evidence required for legal sign-off.
- Flexible items: air-gap is possible, but we recommended private VPC with strict egress controls for faster time-to-production.

What Redwood will provide by 7/18 (deliverables)
- SOC2 summary + attestation pointer (we’ll provide the PDF summary and a secure link to the full report).
- Evidence package: architecture diagram, network zone diagram, recommended IP ranges (redwood-network-ip-ranges.csv), and a short runbook for KMS integration.
- Sample SOW and procurement template (redwood sample-statement-of-work.pdf) — editable for your procurement/legal.
- A connectivity options brief: (1) PrivateLink/Direct Connect pattern with static egress, (2) NAT gateway + static egress IPs, (3) fully air-gapped delivery (cost/time estimate).

Clarifying questions for your infra/legal to help narrow scope:
1) For the KMS ask: will Vela require HSM-backed keys (customer KMS with HSM) or is a managed KMS sufficient?
2) For networking: do you have a preferred connectivity pattern (Direct Connect vs. PrivateLink) or should we propose both with pros/cons?
3) Any specific data retention windows required (archive/purge policies) beyond standard PHI retention?

Attachments we’re sending with this note: Redwood-evidence-package-v1.zip (contains the SOC2 summary stub, architecture diagram, and runbook). We’ll also post the SOC2 link to a secure Drive folder.

I’ll book a 30-minute legal/infra review for next Tue (7/9) — Ben and Priyom are on copy to help scope the SOW. If that date doesn’t work, tell us preferred windows.

Best,

Olga Petrov
Enterprise Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +44 20 7946 0XXX

Subject: Re: Follow-up + compliance checklist (Vela x Redwood)

Thanks, Olga — that looks good. A few quick clarifications from legal/infra before we lock the gate: 
- KMS: we require customer-managed KMS with HSM-backed keys for production PHI.
- Retention: 7-year retention for clinical records, but we can provide a narrower scope for inference logs if you suggest a purge flow.
- Connectivity: preference for PrivateLink if you can guarantee static egress; otherwise Direct Connect is our fallback.

We’ve attached a short summary of regulatory constraints on our end — it highlights where the procurement team will focus (regulatory summary attached). Karen will try to join the Tue slot; if not, we’ll send comments after.

Appreciate the quick turnaround. If you can share the SOW draft and the SOC2 secure link prior to Tue we can have legal start redlining.

— Alex

- Retention: we recommend a separation between inference telemetry (30–90 days by default) and clinical record artifacts (configurable to your 7-year requirement via export hooks). We’ll include recommended purge scripts in the runbook.

I’ve scheduled the 30-minute review for Tue 2028-07-09 10:00 CEST — invite sent to Karen and your infra/legal alias. If you prefer 11:00 or need an alternate day, let us know.
